fields.statement: At 2da4c0b, built rhiza to $TMPDIR and in a scratch repo made six real change sets (accepted, landed, rejected, withdrawn, proposed, draft) via change new/propose/accept/land/reject/withdraw, wrote an interrupted-run journal (dead pid) for each, and ran rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual --once --json with Rex faked as a logger. It reported resumed: [RUNACC] only; the fake rex log has one window new ... run resume RUNACC; only RUNACC.jsonl gained a daemon-resumed entry. Same result with autonomous runs.

At 2da4c0b with the built binary in a scratch repo, rhiza run resume on interrupted runs whose change sets are landed, rejected and withdrawn each exits 3 with 'run X is not resumed: its change set <id> is <state>, no longer accepted' and 'next: rhiza run abandon X'; --json gives code conflict with the same next; cmp shows each journal unchanged.

At 2da4c0b with the built binary, after daemon --once skipped them, rhiza inbox lists one skipped item for each of the landed, rejected, withdrawn, proposed and draft runs ('interrupted, and not resumed: its change set is landed', 'next: rhiza run abandon RUNLND', ...), none for the resumed accepted run; the daemon emitted a blocked OSC 7501 notice per skipped run; rhiza run abandon RUNREJ removes its item. Autonomous runs get no inbox item (pre-existing autonomous exclusion).
